title: Kana'ti and Selu: Game and Corn
subtitle: A family story explaining food and animal origins

narrativeBlocks.title: The lucky hunter and the corn-wife
narrativeBlocks.body: Kana'ti is the great hunter — the game never fails him: he rolls a rock aside and animals pour out for the killing. His wife Selu is the corn-mother: she goes to the storehouse and returns with corn.

narrativeBlocks.title: The boys who watch
narrativeBlocks.body: Their son — and the wild boy they found — spy on their parents: they see Kana'ti's secret cave of game, and they watch Selu produce corn from her own body. The secrets are seen.

narrativeBlocks.title: The game gets loose
narrativeBlocks.body: The boys let the animals out of Kana'ti's cave — the deer and game scatter into the world forever. That is why hunting is hard now: the boys let the easy game go.

narrativeBlocks.title: Selu's sacrifice
narrativeBlocks.body: Selu, knowing they spied on her, says she must die — but tells them to drag her body seven times around the clearing. Where her blood touches the ground, corn grows: the corn-mother becomes the corn.

narrativeBlocks.title: Two gifts in one story
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale explains two Cherokee essentials at once: why the hunt is hard (the escaped game) and why corn grows (Selu's sacrifice) — loss and gift bound together.

quiz.prompt: What happens when the boys spy on their parents?

choices.text: They learn both secrets — then let all the game out of Kana'ti's cave into the world

quiz.explanation: The spying breaks both secrets — and makes hunting hard forever.

quiz.prompt: How does Selu become the corn?

choices.text: She tells the boys to drag her body around the clearing — corn grows where her blood falls
She turns into a corn-stalk in the field
She asks the gods to take her
She plants herself as the first seed

quiz.explanation: The corn-mother's death plants the corn — sacrifice becoming sustenance.
